summary.outcome: Planning completed successfully: 5 plans across 3 waves covering all 6 requirements (including a scope expansion to add batch + drag move), with the plan-checker passing after one revision round. Execution started but the transcript ends mid-Wave 1 (plan 49-01 dispatched, 4 plans remaining).

repo: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — accepts raw sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey, reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case.
`share_keys` entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a move. Download path resolves `k.keyType === 'file' && k.itemId === item.id`.
`adoptSharedFolderResult` must be called only once (for the source result) — calling it for the dest would corrupt the shared folder tree view since the projection filters by shareId only.

Collision policy: `sdkCore.moveItem` throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' (sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:346); propagates through `runWrite` → `p.setError`. No auto-rename needed.

File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from `share_keys keyType:'file-ipns'`, NOT `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` (owner-wrapped, recipient cannot decrypt it) — same pattern as `updateSharedFileHandler`.
`SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) needs both `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` added; currently only lists the 7 Phase 48 methods.

Batch move is a pure web-layer pattern: `useFileBrowserActions` selection Set → `handleBatchMoveConfirm` → `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems`; loops single-item `client.moveItem`. No dedicated SDK batch method.
Drag-and-drop lives in `FileListItem`: `handleDragStart` (multi-select-aware) → drop target on folder rows → `handleDropOnFolder` → `moveItem`/`moveItems`. Shared side has none of this today.
`@internal` on `ensureFolderLoaded` is documentation-only since `CipherBoxClient` is already exported — safe to call directly from the web without adding a new public alias.
`useSharedWriteOps.test.ts` already exists; the fix for the missing REQ-3 unit test was to extend it with a `moveItemHandler` case rather than create a new file.

code.finding: Collision throw: 'An item with this name already exists in destination' — propagates through runWrite

workflow: Sequential wave execution (no parallel worktrees) is the right choice for autonomous/AFK runs — the parallel worktree merge-back protocol is error-prone to hand-drive and the workflow has a documented auto-degrade path for it.

Disabling local commit signing (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) prevents 1Password signer wedging during long AFK runs, but the branch will need a signed rebase or admin override before merge since the repo enforces signed commits on PRs.
The AI-SPEC gate can false-positive on generic keywords like 'eval' from non-AI content (e.g., e2e test requirements) — verify the match before treating it as blocking.
When the plan-checker subagent can't commit (gsd-tools not on PATH), its revision artifacts must be committed manually by the orchestrator after it returns.
UI-SPEC can be skipped (`--skip-ui`) when the new component directly mirrors an existing one with an established design; `gsd:ui-review` can validate retroactively during QA.

Intel API surface (regex extractor) may be empty/unpopulated — it's a HINT-only artifact and can be safely omitted from the planner prompt when RESEARCH.md already carries all verified symbol references.

The plan-checker's finding about vacuous verify passes (a plan's test section lists only files that call through to untested handlers) is a real quality catch worth addressing before execution, not just a doc nit.

Scope expansions mid-planning (before the planner spawns) are low-cost when private-vault analogs exist and can be confirmed quickly — both ROADMAP and CONTEXT must be updated so the planner picks up the new requirements.

friction: Repo enforces signed commits on PRs, but signing had to be disabled locally for the autonomous session — the branch will need a signed rebase or admin override before merge.
